questions.scenario: A test asserts assertEquals(new BigDecimal("1250.00"), account.balance()) and fails with 'expected 1250.00 but was 1250.0', although the amounts are the same.
questions.question: What is the best fix?
options: Compare their toString() values
Use AssertJ's isEqualByComparingTo (compareTo), or normalise money to a fixed scale in the Money type
Convert both values to double before comparing
Remove the assertion
questions.explanation: BigDecimal.equals compares value and scale, so 1250.00 and 1250.0 differ. Comparing with compareTo, or a Money type that fixes the scale, expresses the intended equality; doubles lose precision.

questions.scenario: An interest test passes every day except on the last day of February in leap years, when CI fails at midnight runs.
questions.question: What is the root cause and fix?
options: The code reads the real date (LocalDate.now()); inject a Clock and use fixed clocks in tests, including a leap-year case
Add a retry to the test
The CI server's timezone is wrong; change it
Leap years should be ignored in banking
questions.explanation: Tests that depend on the real clock are non-deterministic. Injecting a Clock lets you test any date, deliberately, every time.

questions.scenario: A unit test for TransferService mocks AccountRepository, FeeCalculator, Money, TransferValidator, the Clock and TransferService itself, and verifies 14 interactions.
questions.question: What is the main problem?
options: It does not mock enough classes
It is over-mocked: it mocks value objects and the class under test and verifies implementation details, so it is brittle and proves little
It should use @SpringBootTest instead
Mockito cannot mock 6 classes at once
questions.explanation: Mock only real boundaries such as repositories, external clients and clocks. Use real value objects and domain collaborators, and assert on resulting state; verify calls only when they are the behaviour.

questions.scenario: A requirement says a debit alert must be sent exactly once for every successful transfer and never for a failed one.
questions.question: Which assertion style suits this requirement?
options: Interaction-based: verify the notifier mock was called once on success, and verifyNoInteractions on failure
Assert on the log output text
Only assert that no exception was thrown
Do not test notifications
questions.explanation: Sending the alert is itself the required behaviour, at a boundary you do not own, so verifying the interaction is appropriate here.

questions.scenario: You are practising TDD on a new 'stamp duty on transfers of ₦10,000 and above' rule.
questions.question: What is the correct first step?
options: Implement the full rule, then write tests
Refactor the fee calculator before writing any test
Write all 20 tests at once, then implement
Write a failing test for a transfer of exactly ₦10,000.00 incurring the duty, and run it to see it fail
questions.explanation: TDD proceeds in small red–green–refactor steps. Seeing the test fail first proves that it can detect the missing behaviour.

questions.scenario: Your unit-test suite takes 9 minutes and fails randomly about once a week.
questions.question: Which changes address both problems? (Choose two.)
options: Run tests in a fixed alphabetical order
Rerun failed tests automatically until they pass
Replace @SpringBootTest with plain unit tests for pure domain logic
Remove shared mutable static state between tests and replace Thread.sleep and now() with injected clocks or Awaitility
questions.explanation: Starting Spring for logic tests is slow, and shared state, sleeps and real time cause flakiness. Rerunning or forcing an order hides the problems instead of fixing them.

questions.scenario: A fee rule has tiers at ₦5,000 and ₦50,000.
questions.question: Which set of test amounts gives the best boundary coverage?
options: ₦5,000 only, because it is the first boundary
A random amount generated on each run
questions.explanation: Bugs cluster at boundaries (< versus <=). Testing exactly on and just past each boundary, plus the smallest valid amount, catches them.
